Is a solo hand management and precision trick-taking game. Your task is to peacefully unite the titular woodland kingdom. You do this by visiting eight fiefs and engaging their rulers in dialogue (tricks) to win them over. You start with four allies, each with an ability that you can use once per visit. These abilities can make you draw, discard, or otherwise manipulate your hand to help you hit the target score. Once you’ve won a ruler over, they can substitute temporarily for one of your allies, giving you more choices for abilities to tackle the harder fiefs! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Play multiple hands of trick-taking. Win an exact number of tricks, aided by your allies' special abilities, to win a hand. Win enough stars from hands to win the game. Contents 1 Game modes 2 Game overview 3 One visit 4 One trick 5 Abilities 6 Game end 7 Important points 8 Game options 9 List of abilities 10 Scenarios Game modes There are two ways to play the game: the standard game, or one of the 16 scenarios. The following are the rules for the standard game. Scenarios put a twist on the standard game; see #Scenarios for more details about them. Game overview The game uses two kinds of cards: dialogue cards and character cards . Dialogue cards are the cards used to play. They come in 4 suits (claws, flowers , leaves , eyes ) and 8 ranks (1-8), for a total of 32 dialogue cards. During the game, dialogue cards will be either in the deck , in your hand , in the discard pile , or in the score pile . Character cards have a suit and a special ability. There are 6 cards in each of the 4 suits, for a total of 24 character cards. All special abilities are unique. There is a row of 8 fiefs . Each fief has a certain number of stars, and requires a specific number of tricks won. From left to right: Stars 4 3 2 1 1 2 3 4 Tricks 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 Each fief begins with a character card, called its ruler . Each ruler is initially neutral to you; your goal is to make them friendly . You begin with 4 character cards, referred to as your allies . The game is divided into 8 visits . Each visit follows the procedure below. One visit Each visit is played following the steps below: 1. Shuffle the dialogue cards, and deal 8 cards as your hand. The rest becomes the deck. 2. Choose an unvisited fief to visit . The suit of its ruler becomes the trump suit for the hand. 3. Choose any number of friendly rulers to temporarily substitute an equal number of your allies. 4. Play tricks until the visit ends. (See #One trick for rules on playing tricks.) 5. If the number of cards in your score pile is exactly the fief's number, you have won the fief. Its ruler becomes friendly to you. Otherwise, you have lost the fief. 6. If you substituted in any ruler (from step 3), remove them from the game. You will begin the next visit with your 4 allies again. If there is still an unvisited fief, repeat this procedure. Thus you will play a total of 8 visits; each fief will be visited exactly once during the game. One trick The bulk of the visit is in playing out tricks. Each trick is played following the steps below: 1. Choose if you want to activate any one special ability. You have access to any ability of allies that you didn't substitute out, as well as any ruler you brought for the hand. Each ability can be activated once during the visit. 2. If your hand or the deck is empty, skip the rest of this procedure. The visit ends (see step 7 below). 3. Place the top card of the deck into the discard pile. This is the ruler's statement . 4. Play a card from your hand. This is your response . You must follow suit if able, i.e. play a card with the same suit as the ruler's statement. If you cannot follow suit, you may play any card from your hand. 5.
